create_refinery_n_reactors.ponder.shared: Closing the nuclear fuel cycle
Cool spent assemblies in the pool, shear them with a mechanical saw, and dissolve the chopped fuel with nitric acid in the existing heated reaction plant.

Each storey is made in Mechanical Crafters and placed as a whole 3 × 3 octagon. Stack twelve behind the drive: two settlers, eight pulse storeys, two settlers. The drive takes at least 32 RPM at its front, dissolved fuel on top and 30 percent TBP solvent on its right.
Four of the pulse storeys are product storeys. From bottom to top they deliver uranium solution, plutonium solution, high-level waste and recycled solvent on any side. Pipe every output away.
Recover PuO₂, mix it with depleted UO₂, press the powder, sinter in hydrogen and assemble MOX rods using zircaloy tubes.
Power the vitrification melter and supply waste, glass frit and an empty canister. Collect the sealed canister.
Feed waste liquid from above, frit and empty canisters through funnels, and extract sealed canisters below. Each placed canister stands 3 m tall.
Blocked outlets stop the batch without consuming feed. Goggles show state; Display Links expose all six fluid inventories, items, heat and progress.
Remote blanket and divertor maintenance
Span the 11 m tokamak with a Fusion Maintenance Crane. The top of the reactor must be within 15 m below the rails.
Switch off the plasma and magnets. Wait for the field to fall below 1% and the blanket to cool to 100 °C or below.
Feed fresh blanket cartridges and tungsten divertor cassettes to the drive using a funnel.
Apply rotation and redstone. The bridge and trolley travel to the nearest point on top of the reactor, lower the handling tool and exchange components with more than 25 percent wear.

create_refinery_n_reactors.ponder.shared: Mixing and casting stainless steel
Superheat six iron ingots, two ferrochrome or chromium and one nickel ingot. The mixer makes 600 mB of molten stainless steel.
A stainless pump sends the molten alloy into the basin under a mechanical press.
Cast 800 mB into one slab. Feed it through a heated tandem rolling mill to obtain eight stainless steel ingots.
Superheat six iron ingots, two ferrochrome or chromium and one nickel ingot. The mixer makes 600 mB of molten stainless steel.
A stainless pump sends the molten alloy into the basin under a mechanical press.
Cast 800 mB into one slab. Feed it through a heated tandem rolling mill to obtain eight stainless steel ingots.
Rolling Thick Steel Plate
Feed one cast steel slab or steel block into the top or back of the feed end.
A short line of 2–3 stands with a lit burner under the feed end rolls plate. With 4–5 stands the same steel becomes beams instead.
Each stand runs about one third faster than the last. Steel forgives ±10% speed error.
Three thick steel plates come out of the outlet.
Thick plate builds pressure tanks and reactor top caps (eight per craft).
Rolling Stainless Clad Plate
Feed a thick steel plate from the top. Put one stainless steel sheet into the right side of the feed end, looking downstream.
Any stand count works. Keep a lit burner under the feed end so the two layers bond hot.
The rolls press the stainless sheet onto the plate. Match the stand speeds within ±10%.
Two clad plates come out: carbon steel inside, stainless skin outside.
Clad plate makes fusion vacuum vessels (sixteen per craft) and stainless tanks (two per craft).
Rolling Lead Sheet
Feed one lead ingot from the top of the feed end.
Lead is soft enough to roll cold: the burner may stay out. Two stands are enough.
Lead forgives ±20% speed error, so it is the easiest stock to learn the mill on.
Two lead sheets come out of the outlet.
Lead sheet lines biological shields (eight per craft) and lead-acid battery casings (four per craft).
Rolling Zircaloy Cladding Tube
Feed three zirconium ingots from the top. Put one nickel ingot into the right side of the feed end, looking downstream.
Any stand count works. Keep a lit burner under the feed end.
Zircaloy forgives only ±6% speed error. Set each stand carefully or the tube stock buckles.
Eight zircaloy cladding tubes come out, twice the crafting-table yield.
Cladding tubes hold the fuel in fuel rods.
Rolling Titanium Sheet
Feed one titanium block from the top of the feed end.
Titanium needs a superheated burner: feed the Blaze Burner a Blaze Cake. Any stand count works.
Titanium forgives only ±4% speed error, the strictest of all stock.
Twelve titanium sheets come out, more than pressing nine ingots.
Titanium sheet goes into low-pressure turbine blades and irradiation cartridges.
Rolling Copper Foil
Feed one copper block from the top of the feed end.
Use 4–5 stands with a lit burner. With only 2–3 stands the block stops at ten copper sheets.
Each stand runs about one third faster than the last; ±10% error is allowed.
Twelve copper foils come out of the outlet.
Copper foil is the negative electrode of a lithium-ion battery: copper and aluminum foil make four casings per craft.
Rolling Aluminum Foil
Feed four aluminum ingots from the top of the feed end.
Use 4–5 stands with a lit burner under the feed end.
Each stand runs about one third faster than the last; ±10% error is allowed.
Twelve aluminum foils come out of the outlet.
Aluminum foil is the positive electrode of a lithium-ion battery: copper and aluminum foil make four casings per craft.
Cold Rolling Electrical Steel
Feed one steel block from the top. Put two quartz into the right side of the feed end, looking downstream, for the silicon.
This is cold rolling: the burner must be out, and the line needs 4–5 stands. A lit burner rolls beams instead.
Cold steel forgives only ±5% speed error.
Six electrical steel sheets come out of the outlet.
Electrical steel cores double fusion motor-generator output: two per craft.
Beating Gold Foil
Feed one gold block from the top of the feed end.
Gold foil needs the full five stands and a lit burner. Four stands refuse the block.
Each stand runs about one third faster than the last; ±10% error is allowed.
Thirty-two gold foils come out of one block.
Gold foil reflects heat in the multi-layer insulation of cryogenic tanks: two per craft.
Rolling Stainless Steel Ingots
Feed one cast stainless slab from the top of the feed end. Cast it from 800 mB of molten stainless steel made in the mixer or the AOD converter.
Any stand count works. Keep a lit burner under the feed end: the slab is rolled hot.
Each stand runs about one third faster than the last; ±10% error is allowed.
Eight stainless steel ingots come out. Rolling is the only way to turn the slab into ingots.
Press the ingots into stainless steel sheets for tanks, pipes and corrosion-proof equipment.
